findings.summary: Production deploy profile double-nests the export landing directory: EXPORT_ROOT=/data/vault/DeepThought while deriveExportPath already appends 'DeepThought/', so exports resolve to /data/vault/DeepThought/DeepThought/<topic-slug>/, contradicting the 2026-08-09 ruling in spec §1.3 that artifacts land at DeepThought/<topic>/. The profile's own comment ('导出件落 <EXPORT_ROOT>/<topic-slug>/') also contradicts src/export.ts:56 and docs/deploy.md:70, so the version-managed production value and the code disagree about who owns the DeepThought path segment.

E3's max_writes assertion has zero discriminating power: profiles/deploy/production.env sets MAX_WRITES=64, which is byte-identical to the built-in default in bin/deep-research-loop.sh:97. If profile loading of MAX_WRITES broke entirely, the built-in default would still satisfy expect(input.max_writes).toBe(Number(prof.MAX_WRITES)). Spec §2 E3 requires the four fields to be proven equal to profile values, and spec §3 discipline states a zero-power check is worse than none; the profile needs a MAX_WRITES value distinct from 64 for this assertion to carry power.

E6's landing-root assertion is tautological with respect to configuration: expect(path.startsWith(`${prof.EXPORT_ROOT}/DeepThought/`)) holds for every possible EXPORT_ROOT value because deriveExportPath unconditionally concatenates vaultRoot + '/DeepThought/'. The check therefore cannot detect the double-nesting defect in the production profile and does not actually verify that the configured root is the intended vault layout.

'--profile' with a missing operand degrades silently instead of failing loudly: the parser assigns PROFILE="${_args[$_i]:-}" (empty when the flag is last), then the empty value falls through to DEPLOY_PROFILE or to no profile at all. A malformed profile selection then either picks up an unrelated environment value or reaches the TICK_CHANNEL refusal without naming the real cause, which undercuts the observability goal of spec §1.1.
